channel.title: Treasure Coast Today
channel.description: Local news for Martin, St. Lucie and Indian River counties, Florida.

item.title: Jensen Beach Park cafe and restroom rebuild expected by late 2027
item.description: Beachgoers at Jensen Beach Park are waiting for the rebuild of the park's restrooms and concession building, which was destroyed in a fire on New Year's Eve in December 2024. The county is currently processing permits and designing the new 9,000 square foot Sea Turtle Beach Cafe.

item.title: St. Lucie County man approved for experimental pancreatic cancer treatment after 62-day wait
item.description: Russell Reed, 64, of St. Lucie County spent 62 days waiting to learn whether he would be approved to receive daraxonrasib, an experimental drug his oncologist believed could help after traditional treatments were no longer effective.

item.title: 28-year-old man dies after weekend double shooting on South 14th Street in Fort Pierce
item.description: A 28-year-old man died Tuesday after he was shot multiple times in Fort Pierce over the weekend. Police say the shooting followed an earlier altercation on Okeechobee Road.

item.title: Vero Beach homeowner may sell home as insurance costs hit $9,000 annually
item.description: Kelly Hagen says her homeowners insurance jumped from $6,000 to $9,000 a year and may force her to sell her Vero Beach home within months if costs continue rising.

item.title: Martin County School District to cut 16 administrative positions, save nearly $4 million
item.description: The Martin County School District plans to eliminate 16 administrative and district-level positions, including three assistant principal positions, and remove 42 unfilled instructional vacancies.

item.title: St. Lucie County Clerk website down for hours after third-party redirection issue
item.description: The St. Lucie County Clerk and Comptroller's website was down for hours Tuesday morning, redirecting visitors to another site before coming back online around 1:30 p.m.

item.title: Fort Pierce owes state nearly $16,000 for operating docks without permits since 2021
item.description: Documents from the Florida Department of Environmental Protection show Fort Pierce has been operating docks on state-owned submerged land at Little Jim Bait & Tackle without required permits since 2021.

item.description: Lionel Messi scored his eighth goal of the tournament and led Argentina to a 3-2 comeback victory over Egypt on Tuesday despite trailing by two goals with only 11 minutes of regulation time remaining. item.title: United States eliminated from World Cup after 4-1 loss to Belgium in round of 16
item.description: Charles De Ketelaere scored twice and assisted on another goal as Belgium defeated the United States 4-1 on Monday night to knock the Americans out of the World Cup.

item.title: IOC ends neutral status vetting for Russian athletes ahead of 2028 Los Angeles Olympics
item.description: The International Olympic Committee advised Olympic sports bodies on Tuesday to end a three-year program vetting Russians for neutral status ahead of qualifying events for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.

item.description:

item.title: FDA recalls frozen Publix GreenWise organic blueberries across eight states including Florida over E. coli risk
item.description: The Food and Drug Administration issued a recall for frozen Publix GreenWise Organic Blueberries due to possible E. coli contamination. The 10-ounce packages were shipped to Publix stores in Florida, Alabama, Georgia, Kentucky, North Carolina, South Carolina, Tennessee and Virginia.

item.title: Florida median-income households need 17 months longer to save for home down payment than in 2016
item.description: A new study by Smart Asset found it now takes the median-income household earner in Florida 17 months longer to save up for a down payment in 2026 than in 2016. For Floridians earning minimum wage of $14 an hour, it takes nearly 26 years to save for a down payment.

item.description: Vision Marine Technologies has announced plans to sell its Palm City property after consolidating operations.

item.description: Andre Leonard Barnes, 66, of Fort Pierce died Tuesday after being shot at a home in the 2700 block of Essex Drive.
